input.quote: (i) The Servicer will indemnify the Issuer, the Owner Trustee and the Indenture Trustee (including in its capacity as Note Paying Agent), and their officers, directors, employees and agents (each, an "Indemnified Person") for all fees, expenses, losses, claims, actions, suits, damages and liabilities (including reasonable legal fees and expenses) resulting from the Servicer's (including in its capacity as Custodian) willful misconduct, bad faith or gross negligence in performing its obligations under the Transaction Documents
input.rationale: Section 6.3 gives us a counterparty-side indemnity: Cellco, as Servicer (including as Custodian) and as Marketing Agent, indemnifies the Issuer and the trustees and their officers, directors, employees and agents for all claims, actions, suits, damages, liabilities and reasonable legal fees resulting from its willful misconduct, bad faith or gross negligence, with standard procedure (prompt notice that is not a condition to recovery absent prejudice, counterparty-funded defence with counsel reasonably satisfactory to the Indemnified Person, separate counsel on conflict, and no settlement without consent), plus survival beyond resignation, termination and trustee removal. The indemnity is uncapped, so it is better than the fallback's 3x super-cap, and there is no reverse indemnity from the Issuer or Depositor anywhere in the agreement (Article IX imposes only perfection, expense and non-petition/limited recourse covenants), so the walk-away risk of a one-way customer indemnity is absent. Two minor points we note but do not redline: there is no IP-infringement limb (immaterial here, as this transfer and servicing agreement involves no vendor deliverables, licensed technology or IP grant), and the Depositor is not itself an "Indemnified Person" under Section 6.3(a), which is consistent with the transaction structure where the Depositor's recourse runs through the originator/transfer documents.
